My research has produced software, technological platforms, digital infrastructures, prototypes, reference implementations, and other artifacts. This page preserves both current work and the technological history behind it.

The registry distinguishes **research projects** from the **technological artifacts** they produce. A project may generate several artifacts, while an artifact may connect multiple projects, publications, students, and institutions.

::: {.software-current-generated}
:::

## Technology as a Research Record

Software is not treated here merely as downloadable code. It is part of the research record: implementations can embody cryptographic protocols, standards, architectural decisions, experiments, and technology transfer.

## Data and Reproducibility

Datasets, experimental results, benchmarks, and reproducibility packages will be incorporated as they are curated. When appropriate, preserved research objects will be linked to persistent repositories and identifiers.

## Preservation Model

The long-term preservation strategy separates three layers:

1. **Development** — source code and active collaboration environments;
2. **Publication** — stable releases associated with papers, projects, and academic outputs;
3. **Preservation** — durable research objects with persistent metadata and, where appropriate, archival repositories and DOIs.

This structure is intended to preserve relationships such as:

`project → software → release → dataset → publication → student → talk`
